articles.title: US approves Musk's SpaceX plan to deploy 1 million satellites for AI data centres in space
articles.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites that will function as data centres
articles.body: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites that will function as data centres in space, as the company seeks to meet rapidly growing demand for artificial intelligence computing.The FCC said on Wednesday it had approved SpaceX's proposed "Starmind" constellation of orbital computing modules which would process massive amounts of data and transmit it back to Earth.SpaceX had earlier sought permission to deploy up to 1 million satellites to support AI computing infrastructure in space.The FCC said the approval would allow SpaceX "to pioneer emergent technology that advances American leadership in space and artificial intelligence".Data centres are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, requiring enormous amounts of electricity to run and cool computing systems.SpaceX has proposed powering its orbital data centres using solar energy, arguing that the technology could significantly reduce energy costs and the environmental impact associated with conventional data centres on Earth."By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance costs, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers," SpaceX told the FCC.The company plans to use its next-generation Starship rocket which is currently under development to deploy the constellation.The ambitious proposal depends heavily on Starship's ability to lower launch costs and carry large numbers of satellites into orbit.FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the approval would help the US strengthen its position in artificial intelligence and expand computing infrastructure."America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence. Under President Trump's leadership, the United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people. The FCC supercharges that effort today by granting, for the first time ever, authorization to deploy 1 million orbital compute modules for data centers in space. This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth," Carr said."Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment. This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," he added.The FCC has also approved SpaceX's request to establish backup communications for its optical network. The system will use radiofrequency links for emergency telemetry, tracking and command operations, as well as backup connectivity across the satellite network.The approval allows communications in the 18.8–19.3 GHz bands for downlinks and 28.6–29.1 GHz bands for uplinks.It remains unclear whether SpaceX will eventually deploy the entire constellation. There are currently around 17,000 satellites in orbit, and deploying 1 million would represent an unprecedented expansion of satellite infrastructure, Reuters reported.Satellite operators often seek approval for larger constellations than they ultimately intend to deploy, allowing flexibility as their technology and business plans evolve.SpaceX had previously sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites. The network currently has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit.Amazon's satellite unit Leo and other competitors have questioned SpaceX's proposed constellation arguing that deploying the entire network could take centuries and that the company may not launch all the satellites it has sought approval for.Carr dismissed the criticism in March, saying, "Amazon should focus on getting Amazon's house in order with their own launches and their own satellite constellation, rather than worrying about other people that are actually out there ​launching satellites at the pace and cadence that SpaceX is."Under the approval, SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033 and launch at least 10% of the approved constellation, or 100,000 satellites by November 2035 and deploy 50% by November 2038.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: US president Donald Trump’s investment portfolios traded shares of chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times between January and September, with the value of his holdings potentially rising by as much as $15 million after the company’s stock surged following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang.A review of Trump’s financial disclosures by BBC Verify found that his portfolios bought between $5.2 million and $17 million worth of Nvidia shares during the first nine months of the year, while selling between $4.4 million and $12 million worth.The filings, submitted to the US Office of Government Ethics, report transactions in broad value ranges rather than exact amounts, making it impossible to establish precisely how much Nvidia stock Trump traded or how many shares he held.Trump’s latest disclosure, submitted on November 5, indicated that he could have held as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30.Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday after the company’s board reinstated Huang as CEO, potentially increasing the value of Trump’s investment by $15 million.The rally followed Trump’s public involvement in Huang’s reinstatement. The president told CNBC he had spoken to Nvidia’s board and “made the deal” to bring the executive back. Nvidia said it had received input from senior US government officials before deciding Huang’s return posed no national security risk.Trump’s portfolios also held between $12.5 million and $58 million worth of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025, according to the disclosures.The White House has said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties, and that neither the president nor his family can direct or influence investment decisions.The frequent trading of Nvidia shares has nevertheless raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, particularly given Trump’s role in the company’s leadership decision and the administration’s oversight of advanced chip exports to China.Nvidia has become one of the world’s most valuable companies amid the boom in artificial intelligence. articles.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei denies wanting humanity to ‘surrender’ free will to AI
articles.summary: Dario Amodei’s remarks come amid predictions that AI may soon match or surpass human intelligence.
articles.body:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has denied believing that humanity should “surrender” control to artificial intelligence amid predictions that models potentially far exceeding human intelligence are imminent.

In a lengthy post on X on Wednesday, Amodei said he does not support surrendering “human free will” to AI and has long argued that the frontier technology should be subject to “legitimate democratic processes”.

“If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years,” Amodei said, responding to an Axios report about a purported “consensus” inside Anthropic that some decision-making authority should be passed to the technology.

“But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.”

Amodei’s remarks come amid a flurry of commentary by top industry executives suggesting that AI will soon match or surpass human intelligence.

The prospect of AI that equals or outperforms the best human minds – referred to as artificial general intelligence (AGI) and artificial super-intelligence (ASI), respectively – has fuelled intense debate in Silicon Valley and beyond about whether such technology can be harnessed for good without exposing humanity to catastrophic harm.

AI safety advocates have raised fears that models being developed by firms such as Anthropic, which made history last week in the biggest initial public offering of all time, could slip out of human control, particularly once systems start improving without human input, a process known as recursive self-improvement.

In his X post, Amodei criticised commentary he said conflated the idea of AI taking over specific tasks with surrendering control in a “grand sense of global governance”.

“This is not AI ‘running the world’, but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end,” Amodei said.

“Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc.”

“It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives,” he added. “But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.”

Citing unnamed sources, Axios reported on Wednesday that Amodei and other Anthropic executives believe it would be irrational “or even unethical” not to hand over authority to AI for tasks it can do better than humans, such as curing diseases.

David Krueger, the founder of Evitable, a nonprofit that campaigns against the development of ASI, said Anthropic should pause its work if Amodei is genuinely concerned about humanity losing control of frontier models.

“We don’t have to consciously surrender control to AI to lose it. As AI becomes increasingly capable, there will be mounting pressure to push humans out of decision-making roles across society,” Krueger told Al Jazeera.

“Meanwhile, researchers at Dario’s own company are warning that AI capabilities are advancing faster than our ability to control them. We need an immediate, indefinite, international moratorium on frontier AI development.”

While there is no universally agreed-upon definition of AGI or ASI, key tech industry figures have over the past week suggested that the milestones are near.

Google DeepMind’s chief AGI scientist and cofounder, Shane Legg, said on Wednesday he believes there is a more than 50 percent chance that “minimal” AGI arrives before 2028.

“We’re getting close now,” Legg said on X.

On Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, said ASI is “arriving” , pointing to the announcement that an Anthropic employee had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.

“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang said on X.

articles.title: RBI continues to bring back gold to India as it repatriates 60 tonnes more of yellow metal, India now houses 84% of its 880.52 metric tonnes gold reserves while remaining are with Bank of England and Bank for International Settlements
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been bringing back India’s gold stored abroad for some time now and it continued to shift the yellow metal reserves
articles.body: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been bringing back India’s gold stored abroad for some time now and it continued to shift the yellow metal reserves back even in this year.However, what is interesting to note is that gold accounted for a smaller proportion of the country's overall foreign exchange reserves at the end of September, data released on Wednesday showed.Despite the increase in gold held within India, its share in total foreign exchange reserves fell to 14.38% at the end of September, compared with 16.7% six months earlier.RBI moves back most of India’s gold reservesAccording to the RBI's latest half-yearly report, India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country.The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.RBI repatriated around 60 tonnes of gold during April-September 2026. India has been progressively repatriating its gold holdings over the past two years amid rising geopolitical risks. In March, 77% of the country's gold reserves were held domestically.India’s forex reservesIndia's foreign exchange reserves totalled $705.3 billion, according to the latest data released by the central bank on Friday.When reserves stood at $668.6 billion at the end of June, they were sufficient to cover 9.8 months of imports, the RBI said.The ratio of short-term debt to foreign exchange reserves climbed to 23% at the end of June 2026, up from 21.6% at the end of March. The ratio of volatile capital flows, including portfolio investments, to reserves also increased, reaching 68% at the end of June against 66.6% three months earlier.Most of India's foreign exchange reserves continue to be invested in securities issued by overseas governments. In addition, $35.95 billion was held as deposits with other central banks and the Bank for International Settlements, while $42.75 billion was deposited with commercial banks abroad."With the objective of exploring new strategies and products in reserve management while diversifying the portfolio, a small portion of the reserves is being managed by external asset managers," the RBI said.The period was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainty, driven by the conflict in West Asia, interruptions to energy supplies and tighter monetary policies adopted by several major central banks.Global gold prices fell by around 9%, with the average price dropping from $4,721 per troy ounce in April 2026 to $4,319 in September."Prices responded to rising US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy. The decline occurred despite continued investor demand for gold as a safe-haven and for portfolio diversification," the report noted.India's overall foreign exchange reserves, meanwhile, grew by $46.67 billion during April-September 2026. They increased from $691.11 billion at the end of March to $737.78 billion at the end of September.Of the $608.26 billion in foreign currency assets held at the end of September, $529.57 billion was invested in securities. A further $35.95 billion was placed with other central banks and the BIS, while $42.75 billion was maintained as deposits with commercial banks overseas.The report also pointed to shifts in the composition of global foreign exchange reserves. The US dollar's share fell from 57.18% in the first quarter of 2026 to 56.70% in the second quarter. Over the same period, the euro's share rose from 20.04% to 20.60%.The RBI reiterated that protecting the safety of India's foreign exchange reserves and ensuring their liquidity remain the central priorities in managing the portfolio, with returns optimised within these parameters.Money habits form by age 7.
